comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the fixed probe merges stderr into the SUCCESS value — a gh warning on a healthy call corrupts the numeric check and rolls back a possibly-live tag**

The lap-3 fix (correct on the failure path) captures both streams into one variable and then uses it as a number:

```bash
probe_out="$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --branch "$tag" --limit 10 \
  --json databaseId --jq 'length' 2>&1)" || { …fail fast… }
if [ "${probe_out:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then …
```

If `gh` exits 0 but writes **anything** to stderr (a deprecation/upgrade notice, a config warning), `probe_out` is no longer a bare integer → `[ … -gt 0 ]` errors (`integer expression expected`, swallowed inside the `if`) → read as "no train" → the full budget burns → and the **rollback deletes the pushed ref while its train may genuinely be running** (the pushed tag was fine; only the probe's output was noisy). That converts a benign warning into a deleted tag and a red train checkout.

Fix: keep stderr out of the success value and surface it only in the failure branch:

```bash
probe_err="$(mktemp)"
if ! probe_out="$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --branch "$tag" --limit 10 \
    --json databaseId --jq 'length' 2>"$probe_err")"; then
  echo "::error::train verification probe failed for $tag (gh run list): $(cat "$probe_err") …" >&2
  rm -f "$probe_err"; exit 1
fi
rm -f "$probe_err"
if [ "${probe_out:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then …
```

The 4th mint test (`GH_STUB_PROBE_FAILS`) covers the non-zero path; worth adding a stub leg for exit-0-with-stderr asserting the train is still recognized.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: a failed mint leaves the orphan tag pushed — the prescribed "re-run" recreates the stranded-draft bug silently**

When the train verification fails (lines 89-99), the tag **has already been pushed** and is left on the remote. The error tells the operator to *"fix the push credential and re-run"* — but that recovery path can never repair the state:

1. attempt 1: push succeeds, no run appears → mint fails loud, leg red, no draft ✓;
2. attempt 2 (re-run): `git ls-remote --exit-code` now finds the tag (rc 0) → **no mint, no extraheader strip needed, no train check** → the caller falls through to the plain `gh release create --draft` → **green leg + a draft attached to a ref whose train never ran** → swept a day later. That is the exact gh-2026 shape (green runs, stranded draft), silently re-armed, and the error message actively instructs the operator into it.

Also note the mint leaves the **local** tag object behind in the checkout between the `git tag -a` and the push/failure — on self-hosted legs with a reused workspace (release-macos/release-mobile), a re-run can additionally die at `git tag -a` with `fatal: tag 'v9.9.9' already exists` (observed in the same reproduction).

Suggested remedy: roll the pushed ref back before failing the verification, so the state before the failed mint is restored and a fixed re-run actually re-mints:

```bash
if [ "$runs_seen" -ne 1 ]; then
  echo "::warning::rolling back the untrained tag ref so a fixed re-run can re-mint" >&2
  git push "${GH_TOKEN:+https://x-access-token:${GH_TOKEN}@github.com/${repo}.git}" ":refs/tags/$tag" \
    || echo "::warning::rollback of refs/tags/$tag failed — a re-run will skip the mint (tag exists) and can strand the draft" >&2
  echo "::error::tag train did not start for $tag: …" >&2
  exit 1
fi
```

(The tiny late-train race — a run appearing just after the budget — is acceptable: the pushed-before-failure window is the same one that today strands drafts for a day.) Alternatively, keep the ref but make the callers verify the train before their plain create too.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the train probe swallows its own failures — a denied probe is indistinguishable from "no train", and the `actions: read` grants don't cover the probe as wired**

`2>/dev/null || echo 0` collapses three different situations into "no train":

1. the push fired nothing (the case this guard exists for);
2. the probe itself failed — 403 (fine-grained `RELEASE_PAT` without Actions:read), expired PAT, rate limit, gh not authenticated;
3. gh exited non-zero for any transient reason.

In case 2/3 the leg burns the full 12×10s budget and then fails with the **"push likely authenticated as a CI-suppressed token"** diagnosis while the real cause (probe denied) was discarded to /dev/null — a misleading RCA on a red release leg.

Note the probe authenticates with **GH_TOKEN (RELEASE_PAT), not the job's GITHUB_TOKEN**: `gh` prefers the `GH_TOKEN` env var, and every mint-reachable call site exports it (enforced by the hygiene lints). The `actions: read` grants added in this PR only govern the job's automatic token, so they neither cause nor fix this — if `RELEASE_PAT` is (or becomes) a fine-grained PAT without Actions:read, **every** mint fails spuriously ~2 minutes in. Nothing in this PR or its tests exercises the probe against the real API (the fixture stubs `gh`).

Suggested remedy — make a probe failure loud and distinct:

```bash
probe_out="$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --branch "$tag" --limit 10 \
  --json databaseId --jq 'length' 2>&1)" || {
  echo "::error::train verification probe failed for $tag (gh run list): $probe_out — distinguish this from 'no train' before blaming the push credential" >&2
  exit 1
}
if [ "$probe_out" -gt 0 ]; then …
```

…and document on the `RELEASE_PAT` secret (and in `docs/ci.md`) that it needs Actions:read for the probe. Please also consider asserting `checked` grants for `build-macos-cli` / `build-extension` in the hygiene test if the intent is that every mint-reachable job carry the grant — the new lint only pins `release-macos` / `release-mobile`, while the lazy legs are the minters most likely to win the race.

```bash
  if git ls-remote --exit-code origin "refs/tags/$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "tag $tag was minted concurrently by a sibling leg — continuing to train verification"
  else
    echo "::error::tag $tag push failed and the ref is still missing" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
fi
```

The loser then proceeds to the train verification, which will see the winner's run and succeed, and its `gh release create` race loss is already tolerated by both callers. Please also add a behavioral test for the raced-mint case to the mint suite (the current 7 tests cover single-minter paths only).
